title: The 10 Best 23-Gauge Pin Nailers
subtitle: Pneumatic 23-gauge pin nailers for trim, cabinets, crafts and glue-ups, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A 23-gauge pin nailer drives headless pins that leave nearly invisible holes, ideal for holding trim and glued parts. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Metabo HPT, DEWALT, Arrow, PORTER-CABLE, Grex and value brands on rating, review volume and features (1-3/8 inch or longer pins, oil-free operation, a dry-fire lockout, depth adjustment and a case). All need an air compressor.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

buyers_guide.q: What is a pin nailer for?
buyers_guide.a: A 23-gauge pinner shoots headless pins so thin the holes almost disappear. Use it to hold trim, moldings and glued parts while the glue dries. Pins have little holding power on their own.
Brad nailers (18 gauge) hold better and are for trim you won't glue. Pin nailers leave smaller holes and won't split thin stock. Many woodworkers own both.

buyers_guide.q: How long a pin do I need?
buyers_guide.a: About twice the thickness of the piece you're attaching. 1-3/8 inch covers most trim. For hardwood face frames and thicker parts, 2-inch pinners like the DEWALT DWFP2350K help.
Oil-free nailers like the DEWALT and Arrow won't spit oil onto finished wood. Oiled nailers need a few drops in the air inlet daily.
Almost any. Pinners use very little air; a small pancake compressor at 70 to 100 PSI is plenty.
